theory.mapping_scope: These annotations explain how source roles are represented by the current Lean model. Device kind, encryption layer and interface zone are separate fields. The local zone represents device-internal interfaces. Device roles remain classified separately. Namespace-local addresses belong to their recorded device, including loopback addresses shared by several devices. Source subtype relationships remain unchanged. Role mappings alone do not establish requirement compliance.

V31-007.title: V31-007: data-plane protection, tunnel endpoints, and services
V31-007.source_text:
Affected groups: RG-007, RG-008, RG-029, RG-030, RG-035. Original pages 10–14, 18–19, 22–25, 42–47. Page 10 requires Inner encryption followed by Outer encryption and reverse Outer/Inner decryption. Pages 12–13 distinguish protected data from permitted control traffic. Arbitrary classified payloads cannot be labelled harmless control.

The selected reading tracks protected payload identities through complete executions. Gray transmission carries Inner protection. Black transmission carries Outer around Inner, with ordered encryption and matching configured endpoints. A completed cross-Black plaintext delivery has ordered reverse decryption. Local Red deliveries that never cross Black do not acquire a fictitious two-decryption duty. The mechanism type admits exactly the four IPsec/MACsec combinations. Outer MACsec restricts the solution to two sites.

The page-22 service clause remains recorded. Under the explicit user optional-management scope, actual management deployment requires its workstations and method-specific CA/KGS infrastructure. Different levels sharing an Outer still require a Gray Firewall. These facts do not gate the packet-transition relation. Management-free packet results have no administrative service-presence prerequisite. The user scope is a stated modeling choice, not a claim that the source's unconditional architectural wording disappeared. Cryptographic confidentiality, integrity, key independence, and faithful operation labels require separately justified primitive and implementation correspondence. Event ordering alone does not establish cryptographic secrecy. Affected declarations: ArchitectureServices, Flow.Valid, CrossedBlack, msc_nested_layer_protection, LayerNoBypass. Inherited decision: INT-007.
V31-007.summary: V3.1 separates encryption mechanism, Inner/Outer layer, interface zone and full security level. Flow.Valid binds the two tunnel endpoints and independent key contexts. AuthenticationServices requires a CA or key-generation service according to each component’s selected authentication method. Workstations are optional under the current scope.

V31-012.title: V31-012: authentication alternatives and management deployment
V31-012.source_text:
Affected group: RG-012. Original page 16, with pages 15–18. Separate CAs, CAKs, and management devices apply to the chosen certificate or shared-key method. Certificate authorities and effective trust closures differ across full levels. PSK identities differ across full levels. Cross-level mutual authentication and established tunnels are both prohibited.

Management presence and separation apply when management is deployed. A packet-only snapshot cannot establish management-device presence. Figure 5 has two Secret U.S.-only networks at the same full level. Different names do not create different levels. Additional same-level filtering is permitted. Inherited decision: INT-012.
V31-012.summary: Credential separation applies to the selected certificate or shared-key method. Management-device presence and separation are required only when managementSelected is true. Different network names do not imply different full security levels.

V31-013.title: V31-013: all Gray paths, filtering, and management services
V31-013.source_text:
Affected group: RG-013. Original pages 17–18, 24, 35. SR-7 covers every physical Gray path between different-level Inners. SR-8 separately names a CA, AW, and CDP/OCSP responder at a different level. The page-18 highest-level convention names Gray AWs and locally run CAs. It does not assign every CDP/OCSP service to the highest level.

The selected reading assigns the highest level to Gray AWs and locally run CAs, retains the broader SR-8 cut for each named service when its actual level differs, and includes enterprise CAs in SR-8. Actual filtering rejects unintended or cross-level Inner endpoints. Highest-group management traffic to lower Inners is rejected. Outer filtering remains mandatory with standalone Gray Firewalls. Gray Firewalls retain classified-device physical protection and placement between Inner and Outer. The word typically does not cancel SR-7 or SR-8. Physical protection and the classification ordering require authoritative external facts.
V31-013.summary: The Gray path specification distinguishes Inner components, Gray Firewalls, workstations, locally run CAs, all CAs and revocation services. Gray AWs and locally run CAs follow the highest-level convention. The broader service-path requirements retain each service’s actual level.

V31-015.title: V31-015: carrier placement and standalone obligations
V31-015.source_text:
Affected group: RG-015. Original pages 19–20, 25, 42. Encapsulation is required when MACsec is Inner or crosses IP. Inner encapsulation precedes Outer encryption. A carrier preserves the MACsec body until its destination. Unsupported built-in encapsulation requires a standalone device with the stated internal/Inner and external/Outer attachments. The protocol needs AO approval.

Pages 19 and 25 impose all applicable Solution Component duties on the standalone device. MD-13 separately confirms Section 11.1 inclusion. Page 20 places the additional step outside the boundary and recommends DM/filtering. Those passages do not cancel the explicit mandatory device duties. Fixed technical meanings and typed external duties replace the caller-supplied catalogue. External records and concrete implementation bindings remain unresolved proof/evidence obligations. The encapsulate event denotes wrapping the exact existing body. Refinement must connect that event to the active carrier operation and the actual remote decapsulator. Inherited decision: INT-015.
V31-015.summary: When built-in encapsulation is unavailable, the selected standalone encapsulator must have the required Inner-side and Outer-side attachments and satisfy its applicable component duties. The current RG-015 definition preserves those duties despite the source passage describing encapsulation as outside the solution boundary.

V31-024.title: V31-024: certificate roles and AS network scope
V31-024.source_text:
Affected group: RG-024. Original pages 14, 20, 26, 41–42. MD-3 and MD-14 are both Threshold alternatives. PSK uses a shared CAK. EAP-TLS uses device certificates, mutual AS admission, MSK-derived CAKs, and both supplicant and authenticator functions at each device. Both functions are supported across arrangements; simultaneity is not imposed.

AA-2 limits the AS to one site network. The ambiguous page-14 both Gray and/or Red wording is read as forbidding one AS from bridging Red and Gray or several site networks. A nonempty attachment list identifies one site and one zone, either Red or Gray. A ban on every Red and every Gray attachment would prevent the described architecture and is rejected.

Key-server peer authentication and SAK issuance remain explicit. Every MACsec encryption history has key-server authentication before SAK issuance. A trust-list entry alone does not prove an EAP-TLS handshake. The implementation connection remains outstanding. Inherited decision: INT024.
V31-024.summary: A MACsec device supports supplicant and authenticator functions across arrangements. EAPRole describes those functions separately from DeviceKind. The AS is bound to one site network in the selected interpretation; one AS must not bridge Red and Gray or several site networks.

V31-027.title: V31-027: key generation, provisioning, central servers, fallback
V31-027.source_text:
Affected group: RG-027. Original pages 20, 29, 41–42. Page 20 explicitly requires all CAKs and CKNs from an NSA-approved KGS while also describing EAP-MSK-derived CAKs. Both duties are retained: an EAP-derived CAK needs an approved generation mechanism. An arbitrary EAP implementation is not assumed approved. Exempting all EAP CAKs from the word all is rejected. Approval remains external.

Each CKN has at least 16 bytes and approved generator provenance. PSK provisioning identifies an authorized Security Administrator obtaining the key before applying it to both endpoints. Each actual tunnel has values 0 and 1 for its key-server pair. A present central management site supplies the server endpoint. The pair central-site declaration must bind the actual deployment; omitting that fact cannot establish the conditional duty.

Fallback means configured alternate CAKs for fallback or rollover. Fresh CAKs from a new authenticated EAP exchange remain permitted. The current INT-MD15-20261024 input was reviewed with the original page-42 row. Its fresh-process and unchanged-configuration assumptions remain explicit. No approval fact is inferred from that interpretation.
V31-027.summary: The key server is an endpoint function. MACsecServerPair and the actual central-management-site declaration determine the server’s placement. Approved key-generation provenance remains an explicit authority condition, including the chosen EAP-derived CAK interpretation.

V31-047.title: V31-047: live sessions and individual credentials
V31-047.source_text:
Affected group: RG-047. Original pages 48–49. Every operation has earlier authentication bound to the same person, component, account, session, and operation token. Logout/revocation invalidates subsequent operations. Selected CNSA/NIST objectives require actual conformity facts in addition to captured flags. Every declared AW administrator has an individual account. AW group accounts are prohibited. Different people have distinct credentials.

A captured certificate identity is not automatically a verified person. Person/account/session ownership and complete lifecycle inventories remain application obligations. Packet behavior does not require an administrative application. Inherited decisions: INT-047-SESSION and INT-047-service-history.
V31-047.summary: Administrative Workstations are optional. When deployed, administrator accounts and active sessions must bind each accepted operation to the appropriate individual and prior authentication. Certificate and NIST objectives add their selected assurance conditions.

V31-056-074.title: V31-056-074: whole-solution protection and redundant duties
V31-056-074.source_text:
Affected groups: RG-056 and RG-074. Original pages 21–25, 36 and the SR-14 footnote. Every physical Red egress crosses a CP-conforming MSC solution or AO-approved data-in-transit solution. Crossing an Inner alone is insufficient. Government-certified and CSfC paths may coexist without an unprotected path.

Every actual redundant solution component retains its fixed applicable CP duties, including Outer Firewalls and selected management components. Ordinary Gray routing infrastructure receives no invented CP security obligation. Standalone encapsulators keep RG-015 duties. Possible failover does not create an automatic availability guarantee. The fixed duty expansion and external assumption boundary remain visible. No whole-group proof completion is claimed.
V31-056-074.summary: Ordinary Gray routing and switching infrastructure has a narrowly defined exemption from component duties. OrdinaryGray requires the matching kind, no encryption layer or infrastructure flag, at least one Gray interface, and only Gray or local interfaces. Standalone encapsulators retain their applicable duties.

V31R-033.title: RG-033: external interface sizes and optional Inner reduction
V31R-033.source_text:
# RG-033: packet size and external-interface limits

The source review uses SR-23 on physical PDF pages 36–37 and IR-2 on pages 42–43. The exact extracted passages are retained in `../proof/RG-033/round-001/source-pages.txt`.

SR-23 requires packet-size configuration that prevents further fragmentation at the external interface of a Gray Firewall or Encryption Component. The selected interpretation includes the Inner encryptor’s Gray-facing interface and the Outer encryptor’s Black-facing interface. Both interfaces are external interfaces of encryption components. The source provides no Inner exclusion. The Gray Firewall’s applicable external interfaces are included as well.

IR-2 adds an optional objective for Inner components: reduce fragmentation and its performance impact while considering Outer and Black limits. That comparison remains separate from the mandatory local MTU bound. The concrete baseline and shared applications leave the optional comparison unselected.

Round 001 exposed an incorrect separation: the mandatory no-further-fragmentation clause selected only the Gray-Firewall/Outer sizing role. The corrected clause also selects the Inner external role. The existing recorded size limits already covered both roles. The correction therefore strengthens the specification and general proof without weakening the recorded checks.

The sizing inventory links each record to the actual device, interface and zone. Inner Gray interfaces use `innerExternal`; Outer Black interfaces and applicable Gray Firewall external interfaces use `grayFirewallOrEncryptionExternal`. These names classify interfaces for the proof. Device kinds and the source ontology remain unchanged.

The accepted interpretation requires a proof about actual represented emissions. A stored MTU or a count of sizing records alone cannot establish the requirement. Source preparation, subsequent processing, header and encryption overhead, and final transmission must satisfy the corresponding size bounds. The instantiated applications cover the selected IPv4/IPsec processing model and retain its explicit implementation assumptions.
V31R-033.summary: Mandatory MTU bounds include Inner Gray interfaces, Outer Black interfaces and applicable Gray Firewall external interfaces. The separate Inner fragmentation-reduction objective remains optional.

def IndependentComponents (records : TechnicalDutyRecords) (d : Deployment) : Prop :=
  ∀ inner ∈ d.devices, inner.layer = some .inner →
    ∀ other ∈ d.devices, (d.Relevant inner.id ∨ d.Relevant other.id) →
    other.layer = some .outer ∨ other.kind = .grayFirewall →
    ∀ first ∈ records.components, ∀ second ∈ records.components,
      first.component = inner.id → second.component = other.id →
      first.physicalDevice ≠ second.physicalDevice ∧
      (IndependentManufacturers first second ∨
        (first.product ≠ second.product ∧ records.external.Confirms
          .nsaIndependenceApproval (.componentPair inner.id other.id))) ∧
      (other.layer = some .outer →
        first.operatingSystemFamily ≠ second.operatingSystemFamily ∧
        IndependentCryptographicLibraries records first second)

RG-007.title: Two independent encryption layers and allowed tunnel pairings
RG-007.translation: Every modeled trace must use the declared Inner and Outer tunnel pairing for protected Red payloads. Gray transmission carries the Inner layer; Black transmission and reception carry both layers. Inner encryption precedes Outer encryption, and receiving-side decryption removes Outer before Inner. The definition also requires complete model coverage, independent key contexts, suitable peer placement, and the required authentication and architecture services.

references.label: msc_nested_layer_protection
CoreReq_msc_nested_layer_protection
references.code:
def CoreReq_msc_nested_layer_protection {S A : Type} (d : Deployment) (model : ForwardingModel S A)
    (flows : List Flow) (flowOf : S → List A → S → PayloadId → Flow) (independentKeys : String → String → Prop) : Prop :=
  model.CoversDeployment d ∧ ArchitectureServices d ∧
  (∀ flow ∈ flows, flow.Valid d independentKeys) ∧
  (∀ start actions finish, model.initial start → model.system.MTr start actions finish →
    let events := model.TraceEvents actions
    let selectedFlow := flowOf start actions finish
    (∀ payload network, .inject payload network ∈ events →
      selectedFlow payload ∈ flows ∧ (selectedFlow payload).sourceNetwork = network) ∧
    (∀ earlier later payload iface layers trafficClass,
      events = earlier ++ [.transmit payload iface layers trafficClass] ++ later →
      model.ProtectedPayload d payload →
      ∀ interface ∈ d.interfaces, d.Relevant interface.device → interface.id = iface →
      (interface.zone = .gray → selectedFlow payload ∈ flows ∧ layers = [(selectedFlow payload).innerTunnel] ∧
        .encrypt payload (selectedFlow payload).innerTunnel ∈ earlier) ∧
      (interface.zone = .black → selectedFlow payload ∈ flows ∧
        layers = [(selectedFlow payload).outerTunnel, (selectedFlow payload).innerTunnel] ∧
        Before earlier (.encrypt payload (selectedFlow payload).innerTunnel)
          (.encrypt payload (selectedFlow payload).outerTunnel))) ∧
    (∀ payload iface layers trafficClass, .receive payload iface layers trafficClass ∈ events →
      model.ProtectedPayload d payload →
      ∀ interface ∈ d.interfaces, d.Relevant interface.device → interface.id = iface → interface.zone = .black →
      selectedFlow payload ∈ flows ∧
      layers = [(selectedFlow payload).outerTunnel, (selectedFlow payload).innerTunnel]) ∧
    ∀ earlier later payload network layers,
      events = earlier ++ [.deliver payload network layers] ++ later →
      .inject payload (selectedFlow payload).sourceNetwork ∈ earlier → CrossedBlack d earlier payload →
      selectedFlow payload ∈ flows ∧ network = (selectedFlow payload).destinationNetwork ∧ layers = [] ∧
      Before earlier (.decrypt payload (selectedFlow payload).outerTunnel)
        (.decrypt payload (selectedFlow payload).innerTunnel))

    (use.builtInSupported = false → d.standaloneEncapsulator use.encapsulator ∧
      d.OwnedGrayAttachment use.inner use.encapsulator use.inputInterface ∧
      (∀ outer, use.outer = some outer →

      d.Relevant use.remoteEncapsulator) → ∀ payload,

        events = earlier ++ [.transmit payload use.outputInterface layers trafficClass] ++ later →
        .encapsulate payload use.encapsulator use.protocol ∈ earlier) ∧

        events = first ++ [.encapsulate payload use.encapsulator use.protocol] ++ middle ++

    (∃ use ∈ observations.uses, binding.InScope use) ∧
    ∀ use ∈ observations.uses, binding.InScope use →

references.code:
def TimeServiceRecord.ValidUse (record : TimeServiceRecord)
    (observations : TimeObservationInventory) (d : Deployment) (zone : Zone)
    (binding : TimeClockBinding) (use : TimeClockUse) : Prop :=
  record.binding = binding.id ∧ use.binding = binding.id ∧ binding.InScope use ∧
  use.clock = binding.clock ∧ use.clockKind = binding.clockKind ∧ use.process = binding.process ∧
  use.executable = binding.executable ∧
  record.source.Bound d zone ∧ observations.runtime.sourceTrusted record.source ∧
  ∃ configuration ∈ observations.configurations,
    configuration.id = record.configuration ∧
    use.configuration = configuration.id ∧ configuration.clock = binding.clock ∧
    configuration.source = record.source ∧ configuration.adjustmentEnabled = true ∧
    configuration.observer = binding.observer ∧ binding.operatingFrom ≤ configuration.order ∧
    use.source = record.source ∧
    (match configuration.maximumRemainingCorrectionNanoseconds with
      | none => True
      | some maximum => ∃ offset, use.remainingCorrectionNanoseconds = some offset ∧
          offset.natAbs ≤ maximum) ∧
    (match configuration.maximumSkewMilliPpm with
      | none => True
      | some maximum => ∃ skew, use.skewMilliPpm = some skew ∧ skew ≤ maximum) ∧
    ∃ update ∈ observations.updates,
      update.id = record.update ∧ use.update = update.id ∧
      update.configuration = configuration.id ∧ update.clock = binding.clock ∧
      update.source = record.source ∧ update.operation.Valid ∧
      update.process = configuration.synchronizerProcess ∧
      (match update.operation with
        | .correction _ _ => True
        | .discipline process => process = configuration.synchronizerProcess) ∧
      update.observer = binding.observer ∧ configuration.order < update.order ∧
      update.order < use.order ∧
      (∀ later ∈ observations.updates, later.clock = binding.clock →
        later.observer = binding.observer → later.order ≤ use.order →
        later.order ≤ update.order) ∧
      ∀ invalidation ∈ observations.invalidations, invalidation.clock = binding.clock →
        invalidation.observer = binding.observer →
        ¬ (update.order ≤ invalidation.order ∧ invalidation.order ≤ use.order)

def AuditRetentionConfiguration (records : TechnicalDutyRecords) (component : String) : Prop :=
  (∀ event ∈ records.audits, event.component = component →
    event.time + 365 * 86400 ≤ event.retainedUntil ∧
    ∃ backup ∈ event.backedUpAt, event.time ≤ backup) ∧

    (∀ year quarter,

      ∃ checked ∈ storage.capacityCheckedAt,

        checked < CalendarQuarterEnd year quarter ∧
        storage.operatingFrom ≤ checked ∧ checked ≤ storage.operatingUntil) ∧
    storage.warningOnLowSpace = true ∧ storage.offloadEnabled = true ∧
    storage.overflowHandling ≠ "" ∧ storage.powerLossHandling ≠ "") ∧

class_semantics: A class describes entities matching an extracted role or realization concept. Classes may overlap and may have multiple parents. No device existence, class disjointness, or class equivalence is asserted.
association_semantics: Non-subtype links are OWL annotation assertions between class IRIs. They preserve source context without imposing object-property restrictions or asserting a relationship for every class member.

nodes.label: Extracted role or concept realization
nodes.description: Analyst-defined organizational superclass for realizations of the role and concept categories extracted from the CSfC MSC v1.3.0 source. Each role class denotes the entities or bearers that realize its source-context category. The categories include devices, services, aggregates, mixed authorities, and protocol functions. The root does not reproduce a CP definition and does not assert that every category is a physical device or an MSC Solution Component. Classes without a curated parent receive a generated organizational edge to the root; that edge is separate from source-backed subtype evidence.

nodes.label: Intrusion Prevention System
nodes.description: Optional product-selection category in MSC-PS-5.

theory.meaning: Intrusion Prevention Systems have a dedicated device kind.

nodes.label: Host/server for AW virtual machines
nodes.description: Physical host/server used to host management or AW virtual machines; restrictions preserve dedicated functions.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define the host/guest virtualization or physical-workstation realization hierarchy. The source role remains available for future modeling.

nodes.label: Virtual Machine
nodes.description: Virtual implementation form for management services and AWs.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define the host/guest virtualization or physical-workstation realization hierarchy. The source role remains available for future modeling.

nodes.label: Physical workstation
nodes.description: Physical implementation form; may host an AW or another explicitly separated function.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define the host/guest virtualization or physical-workstation realization hierarchy. The source role remains available for future modeling.

nodes.obligation_note: The association concerns machines used for Administrative Workstations.

nodes.label: Enrollment server
nodes.description: Enrollment function mentioned in restrictions on cohosting management functions.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define a separate role or protocol model for this certificate-provisioning function.

nodes.label: Provisioning server
nodes.description: Provisioning function that must be separated from AW functions.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define a separate role or protocol model for this certificate-provisioning function.

nodes.label: Certificate registration component
nodes.description: Certificate-registration function separated from AW functions; exact product is unspecified.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define a separate role or protocol model for this certificate-provisioning function.

nodes.label: Registration Authority
nodes.description: Mixed hardware, software, and personnel authority collecting and submitting certificate information; device realization is unspecified.

theory.meaning: V3.1 does not define a separate role or protocol model for this certificate-provisioning function.

nodes.label: Trusted time source
nodes.description: Trusted time source on the Red Network for Red components or on the Gray Management Network for Gray components.

theory.meaning: A time-source endpoint records the actual source component and interface. Placement and client synchronization use the time model.

nodes.label: DNS server
nodes.description: Server referenced through configured DNS server addresses; not assigned an explicit deployment location.

theory.meaning: DNS service use is represented by the name-resolution management function and configuration records. DeviceKind has no separate DNS-server constructor.

nodes.label: Control plane network service
nodes.description: Inside-network service category; NTP is an example rather than a new named device instance.
aliases: Network services provided by control plane

theory.meaning: Control service registrations identify protocol and port. Their kind is recorded separately from the hosting device.

nodes.label: Third-party server
nodes.description: External server contact category blocked or disabled for Outer Encryption Components.

theory.meaning: Third-party behavior is represented by feature and emitted-traffic records. The remote server is not a dedicated device kind.

nodes.obligation_note: RG-037 constrains Outer components that could contact the server. The obligation is enforced at the Outer component.

nodes.label: End user device
nodes.description: Device category in combined CSfC solutions referenced by MSC-SR-13.

theory.meaning: Red network records and modeled payload origins identify source and destination networks. DeviceKind has no separate end-user-host constructor.

nodes.obligation_note: These are associated network protection and combined-solution duties. The current role model does not represent a distinct end-user-device kind.

nodes.label: High Assurance encryptor
nodes.description: Example approved protection for remote administration; not equated to an MSC encryption component.

theory.meaning: The extracted assurance/product category is not a distinct device kind in v3.2. Product eligibility and external assurance remain separate evidence obligations.

nodes.obligation_note: The Red-egress specification accepts an authority-approved alternative protection path. It does not formalize the internals of a High Assurance encryptor.

nodes.label: NSA-certified Government-off-the-Shelf product
nodes.description: Alternative approved egress product in the MSC-SR-14 footnote.

theory.meaning: The extracted assurance/product category is not a distinct device kind in v3.2. Product eligibility and external assurance remain separate evidence obligations.

nodes.obligation_note: The Red-egress specification accepts authority-approved alternative protection. It does not establish product certification.

nodes.label: Locally Managed Device
nodes.description: Management-mode role defined by a hardwired AW connection.

theory.meaning: Administrative operation and connection records describe management access. V3.1 does not divide devices into local-management and remote-management kinds.

nodes.label: Remotely Managed Device
nodes.description: Management-mode role defined by methods other than a local hardwired AW connection.

theory.meaning: Administrative operation and connection records describe management access. V3.1 does not divide devices into local-management and remote-management kinds.

nodes.label: Auxiliary network device
nodes.description: Generic supporting device category in Security Administrator duties.

theory.meaning: The broad source grouping has no dedicated v3.2 role predicate. Specific member functions must be mapped separately.

nodes.obligation_note: The shared case records the administrator duty to defend auxiliary devices; it does not assign them a separate packet-processing specification.

nodes.label: Infrastructure authentication service
nodes.description: Service used for access to infrastructure components under MSC-GD-27; not assumed identical to the MACsec AS.

theory.meaning: Authentication is a registered service function hosted by a component. The hosting device may also have the authenticationServer kind.

nodes.label: Network administration device
nodes.description: Generic administrative device wording in MSC-DM-7; correspondence with AW is not explicitly defined.

theory.meaning: The source role may be realized by workstation or administration services. V3.1 has no separate network-administration-device kind.

nodes.label: Infrastructure component
nodes.description: Generic infrastructure category in password, authentication-service, inventory, and inspection requirements.

theory.meaning: The device record has an infrastructure flag. Flow.Valid requires both encryption endpoints to carry that flag.

nodes.label: Network device
nodes.description: Generic device category used in DNS-service restrictions and protocol discussion.

theory.meaning: Device is the general inventory record for all modeled device kinds. Source role membership beyond that inventory remains contextual.

nodes.label: Perimeter device
nodes.description: Outer Encryption Component placement facet when no Outer Firewall is present.

theory.meaning: The broad source grouping has no dedicated v3.2 role predicate. Specific member functions must be mapped separately.

nodes.label: Key and certificate management component
nodes.description: Component category whose detailed requirements are relocated to separate annexes.

theory.meaning: Key management combines CA and key-generation device records, service functions, and component-to-service relations.

nodes.label: Trust Anchor CA
nodes.description: CA whose certificate is installed as the trust anchor under MSC-VG-4; Root CA remains a separately preserved example rather than an exact alias.

theory.meaning: The authentication model records certificate issuers and trusted issuer identifiers. It does not encode the full CA hierarchy or every distinction among these source roles.

nodes.label: Approved password generator
nodes.description: Generates passwords as recommended by MSC-GD-21; the document does not specify a hardware or software realization.

theory.meaning: Password-generator approval is an external configuration/authority requirement. V3.1 has no separate password-generator behavior model.

nodes.obligation_note: The shared case records a secret-entropy threshold or a domain-authentication alternative. It does not prove how a password generator produces its output.

nodes.label: Log and status repository
nodes.description: Receives logs and status information as an alternative to a SIEM; its implementation is unspecified.

theory.meaning: Logging and monitoring registrations represent the service role. A repository-specific device kind is not required by the model.

nodes.label: Testing equipment
nodes.description: Equipment available for gray-box testing inside and outside the developed solution; no particular product is specified.

theory.meaning: These source roles describe the testing process. V3.1 does not formalize them as network device roles.

nodes.obligation_note: The shared case requires externally supplied testing confirmations. The code does not model the testing equipment itself.

nodes.label: Testing software
nodes.description: Software available for gray-box testing inside and outside the developed solution; no particular product is specified.

theory.meaning: These source roles describe the testing process. V3.1 does not formalize them as network device roles.

nodes.obligation_note: The shared case requires externally supplied testing confirmations. The code does not model the testing software itself.

nodes.label: IKEv2 initiator
nodes.description: Protocol endpoint role that sends the initiator messages in the described IKE_SA_INIT exchange. The source does not identify Bob or Alice as that endpoint.

theory.meaning: The retained model records tunnel and authentication endpoints. It does not introduce an IKE initiator/responder role type; ManagementExchange.responder concerns management traffic.

nodes.obligation_note: These VPN authentication, algorithm, and rekey conditions concern the exchange. The current role model has no separate IKE initiator type.

nodes.label: IKEv2 responder
nodes.description: Protocol endpoint role that sends the responder messages in the described IKE_SA_INIT exchange. The source does not identify Bob or Alice as that endpoint.

theory.meaning: The retained model records tunnel and authentication endpoints. It does not introduce an IKE initiator/responder role type; ManagementExchange.responder concerns management traffic.

nodes.obligation_note: These VPN authentication, algorithm, and rekey conditions concern the exchange. The current role model has no separate IKE responder type.

excluded_inferences.claim: Locally run CA and Enterprise CA are disjoint classes.
excluded_inferences.reason: The source offers operating/management choices without establishing a universal logical partition of CA realizations.

excluded_inferences.claim: Every CA is a Solution Component.
excluded_inferences.reason: The source conditionally says CAs can be part of an MSC Solution and permits enterprise CAs outside Solution Owner management. The general CA category is broader than the explicitly scoped component subclasses.

excluded_inferences.claim: Every AW is a Solution Component.
excluded_inferences.reason: The source also mentions prohibited Black AW management. Positive MSC component membership is asserted for Red and Gray AW specializations only.

excluded_inferences.claim: Supplicant, Authenticator, IKEv2 initiator, and IKEv2 responder are physical-device subclasses.
excluded_inferences.reason: The authentication passage describes performed functions. The IKE exchange passage describes protocol endpoint roles without defining physical-device categories or identifying the named illustrative participants.

excluded_inferences.claim: AW is universally a Virtual Machine or Physical workstation, or the AW host is the AW.
excluded_inferences.reason: The source permits alternative realizations and distinguishes the physical host/server from hosted VMs.

excluded_inferences.claim: Outer Encryption Component is universally a Perimeter device.
excluded_inferences.reason: The source makes the perimeter-device role conditional on Outer Firewall absence.

excluded_inferences.claim: Red or Gray Management Services are subclasses of their Management components.
excluded_inferences.reason: The source describes aggregates composed of components. Composition does not imply subclass membership.

excluded_inferences.claim: A device that administers another category inherits that category.
excluded_inferences.reason: The Red and Gray AW descriptions assign administration of encryption components, firewalls, and services. Those functional relationships do not establish class inclusion.

excluded_inferences.claim: Registration Authority is equivalent to Certificate registration component or is a physical-device subclass.
excluded_inferences.reason: The RA definition collectively includes hardware, software, and people; the cohosting passages mention certificate registration functions without equating the terms.

excluded_inferences.claim: Source aliases, example alternatives, and UI families define equivalent or disjoint OWL classes.
excluded_inferences.reason: Lexical aliases, examples, and navigation groups do not establish equality or a logical partition. No equivalence, disjointness, or exhaustive covering axiom is introduced.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p010:u005.s0.text: The two encryption tunnels protecting a data flow can use either Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) generated by a Virtual Private Network (VPN) Gateway or Media Access Control Security (MACsec) generated by a MACsec Device.
VPN Gateways and MACsec Devices are implemented as part of the network infrastructure.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p010:u006.s0.text: Throughout this CP, the term “Encryption Component” refers generically to either a VPN Gateway or a MACsec Device.

“Inner Encryption Component” refers to the component that terminates the Inner layer of encryption and “Outer Encryption Component” refers to the component that terminates the Outer layer of encryption.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p010:u007.s0.text: As shown in Figure 1, before being sent across the untrusted network, each packet or frame of classified data is encrypted twice; first by an Inner Encryption Component, and then by an Outer Encryption Component.
At the other end of the data flow, the received packet is correspondingly decrypted twice; first by an Outer Encryption Component, and then by an Inner Encryption Component.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p011:u005.s0.text: The Red Network is logically located behind an Inner Encryption Component.
Red Networks are under the control of the Solution Owner or a trusted third party using a Red Administrative Workstation (AW).
The Red AWs maintain, monitor, and control all security functions for the Inner Encryption Components, Inner Firewall, and all Red Management Service Components.
The Red AWs are not permitted to maintain, monitor, or control Outer Encryption Components or Gray Management Services.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p011:u007.s0.text: Gray Networks are composed of Gray data and Gray Management Services.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p011:u009.s0.text: Gray Network components consist of the Outer Encryption Component, Gray Firewall, and Gray Management Services.
Gray Management Services are physically connected to the Gray Firewall and include, at a minimum, a AW that can be a physical workstation or Virtual Machine (VM).

The Gray Management Services may also include a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) unless the SIEM is implemented in the Red Network in conjunction with a cross domain solution (CDS) (see CSfC Continuous Monitoring Annex).
This CP requires the management of Gray Network components through a Gray AW.
As a result, neither Red nor Black AWs are permitted to manage the Outer Encryption Component, Gray Firewall, or Gray Management Services.
Additionally, the Gray AWs are prohibited from managing Inner Encryption Components.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p012:u001.s0.text: Inner Encryption Components must be managed from a Red AW.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p012:u003.s0.text: The network connecting the Outer Encryption Components together is a Black Network.
As shown in Figure 2, if the Black Network is an untrusted network such as the Public Internet, an Outer Firewall is required between the Black Network and the Outer Encryption Component.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p012:u007.s0.text: Management plane traffic is used to configure and monitor Solution Components.
It includes the communications between a system administrator and a component, as well as the logs and other status information forwarded from a Solution Component to a SIEM, or similar repository.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p013:u006.s0.text: Restrictions are also placed on control plane traffic for the Outer Encryption Component.
The Outer Encryption Component is prohibited from implementing routing protocols on external and internal interfaces.
The Outer Encryption Component may not perform routing functionality.
If an Outer Firewall is present, the Outer Firewall can perform routing functions.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p014:u001.s0.text: Here, each Red Network has two Encryption Components associated with it; an Inner Encryption Component connected to the Red Network, and an Outer Encryption Component between the Inner Encryption Component and the Black Network.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p014:u002.s0.text: There are two layers of encryption tunnels between any pair of sites communicating directly with one another; one encryption tunnel between their Outer Encryption Components, and a second encryption tunnel between their Inner Encryption Components.
Each set of Inner or Outer Encryption Components can provide encryption using either IPsec or MACsec.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p014:u006.s0.text: For independently managed sites, each site performs the administration of its own Encryption Components.

If Certification Authorities (CAs) are part of the MSC Solution, each site has the option to use either locally run CAs that they manage and control or, where available, enterprise CAs that are not necessarily managed by the Solution Owner.
Each site needs to ensure that the Encryption Components selected interoperate with those at the other sites.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p014:u007.s0.text: In the MSC Solution, Encryption Components at each site using public key certificates need to have the signing certificates and revocation information for the corresponding CAs used by the other sites.
This high-level design requires cooperation between the various sites in the solution to ensure that all CAs used by each site are trusted at all the other sites.
Similarly, MACsec Devices using a Connectivity Association Key (CAK) need to have the same CAK used by the other site in the MSC Solution.
If MACsec Devices are authenticating using certificates, the authentication server (AS) must not connect to both Gray and/or Red Networks.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p015:u002.s0.text: At least two CAs are needed; one for all the Inner Encryption Components and one for all the Outer Encryption Components.
If available, enterprise CAs should be used.

If MACsec Devices are used on either or both layers and EAP-TLS is used for authentication, then CAs and an AS located at the Central site are required, otherwise, PSKs may be used for authentication for one of the layers of the solution and that layer would not require a CA.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p015:u004.s0.text: Because the central management site manages the Encryption Components at the other sites over the network, encryption is used to logically separate data and management traffic as it passes between sites.
Red management traffic is encrypted before being routed through the Inner and Outer Encryption Components to another site.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p015:u007.s0.text: Although each Red Network requires its own Inner Encryption Component, a site may use a single Outer Encryption Component to encrypt and transport traffic that has been encrypted by Inner Encryption Components of varying security levels.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p016:u001.s0.text: An unclassified network can also be included behind the Outer Encryption Component but must be behind its own Inner Encryption Component and meet the requirements in this CP as if it was a Red Network.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p016:u002.s0.text: Given both cases, separate CAs, CAKs, and management devices are needed to manage the Inner Encryption Components at each security level.

For example, Figure 5 shows a Central Management Site (Site A) and a Remote Site (Site B), but network 1 and network 2 each has its own Red Management Services, which prevents the Inner Encryption Components of the two networks from being able to authenticate with one another.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p016:u004.s0.text: When Red Networks that operate at the same security level are implemented, the cryptographic separation provided by the Inner Encryption Components is sufficient to protect against unintended data flows between the two networks.

Two Inner Encryption Components for networks of different security levels will be unable to mutually authenticate with each other because they trust different CAs that do not have a trust relationship with one another or they use different CAKs that will not provide authentication.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p017:u005.s0.text: Any physical path through a Gray Network between multiple Inner Encryption Components supporting Red Networks of different security levels must include at least one filtering component.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p017:u006.s0.text: When multiple security levels are used, it is critical to enforce proper IP address assignment and firewall rule sets.

The IP address assigned must be unique to that security level such that each network’s Inner Encryption Component is only able to send and receive traffic to its respective Inner Encryption Component at the other site.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p018:u001.s0.text: Additionally, filtering components are included between the components used for management of the Gray Networks themselves (namely, AWs and locally run CAs) and Inner Encryption Components that support Red Networks of a lower security level than the Red Network with the highest security level supported by the solution.
In other words, AWs and locally run CAs on Gray Networks are treated as, and grouped with, the Inner Encryption Component for the Red Network with the highest security level.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p018:u002.s0.text: One or more Gray Firewalls must be included in the Gray Network to perform filtering.

Standalone Gray Firewalls have been placed at each site between the Inner Encryption Components and the Outer Encryption Component; these Gray Firewalls are responsible for dropping packets between Inner Encryption Components of different security levels.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p018:u004.s0.text: Figure 6 also shows an example placement of Gray Firewalls, as long as any path between Inner Encryption Components for networks of different security levels includes a Gray Firewall.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p018:u005.s0.text: Including one or more standalone Gray Firewalls in a solution does not remove the requirement to perform the filtering on the Outer Encryption Component as well.

Outer Encryption Components are uniquely positioned to block traffic between Inner Encryption Components supporting Red Networks of different security levels when one of those Inner Encryption Components is located at a different site.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p018:u007.s0.text: An IPsec tunnel is established between VPN Gateways.
A MACsec tunnel is established between MACsec Devices.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p019:u008.s0.text: The MACsec-encrypted traffic needs to be encapsulated if the MACsec Device is the first layer of encryption in the MSC Solution or if the MACsec-encrypted traffic needs to traverse an IP-based network.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p019:u009.s0.text: In some commercial MACsec Devices, encapsulation can be applied on the internal interface by creating a pseudowire (see Figure 7), which emulates a point-to-point connection.
If this feature is not supported, a standalone device is needed to encapsulate the MACsec-encrypted data (see Figure 8).
If using a standalone device, the internal interface will be connected to the Inner MACsec Device and the external interface will be connected to the Outer Encryption Component.
Since this device resides in the Gray Network, all requirements for Solution Components must be implemented.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u002.s0.text: When the Inner Encryption Component is a MACsec Device the traffic requires additional encapsulation before it is passed through the Outer Encryption Component to the Black Network.
This additional step falls outside the boundary of the MSC Solution.
However, it is highly recommended to apply the general device management (DM) and port filtering requirements for Solution Components.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u003.s0.text: If supported in the MACsec Device, this CP allows VLAN ID tags to be used in the clear.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u004.s0.text: At high speeds (100 GB/s or higher), some MACsec Devices may be configured to use an extended Packet Number (XPN), as described in IEEE 802.
If supported in the MACsec Device, this CP allows the XPN feature to be used.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u006.s0.text: The MSC Solution provides mutual device authentication between Outer Encryption Components and between Inner Encryption Components.
The method of authentication is different for VPN Gateways and MACsec Devices.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u007.s0.text: VPN Gateways authenticate via public key certificates.

VPN Gateways may also implement Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Request for Comments (RFC) 8784-compliant IKEv2 and use Pre-Shared Key (PSK) in addition to public key certificates to provide quantum resistant confidentiality.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u008.s0.text: MACsec Devices authenticate using a PSK called a CAK or using EAP-TLS over 802.
For each MACsec tunnel, a Key Server is identified.
The Key Server authenticates the other MACsec Device and issues a Secure Association Key to provide confidentiality and integrity for the MACsec tunnel.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p020:u009.s0.text: This CP requires all authentication certificates issued to VPN Gateways and MACsec Devices to be Non- Person Entity certificates.
This CP also requires all CAKs and their associated Connectivity Key Names (CKNs) to be generated using an NSA-approved Key Generation Solution (KGS).

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p021:u004.s0.text: Multicast messages received on external interfaces of the Outer Encryption Component must be dropped.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p021:u008.s0.text: Figure 9 shows an MSC Solution between two sites where each site has a redundant Outer Encryption Component (Management components are omitted from the figure for clarity).
There are two outer encryption tunnels that transit the Black Network: one between the upper pair of Outer Encryption Components, and one between the lower pair of Outer Encryption Components.
Each site’s Gray Network contains an ordinary router between the Inner and Outer Encryption Components that selects which Outer Encryption Component to route outbound packets.
This router is part of the solution only in the sense that it is part of the network infrastructure of the Gray Network; this CP does not levy any security requirements on the router/switch.
The MSC Solution can maintain connectivity between the two sites even if one of the Outer Encryption Components fails because traffic will be routed through the tunnel that has not failed.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p022:u001.s0.text: MSC Solution with Redundant Outer Encryption Components

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p022:u002.s0.text: Implementing standby or failover Encryption Components, performing load balancing between Encryption Components, or other techniques to improve the availability or throughput of the solution are outside the scope of this CP and are not discussed further.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p022:u004.s0.text: 2, all communications flowing across a Black Network are protected by at least two layers of encryption, implemented using IPsec tunnels generated by VPN Gateways or MACsec tunnels generated by MACsec Devices.

Mandatory aspects of the solution also include AWs, CAs for key management using Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), a KGS for generating pre- shared CAKs, and Gray Firewalls when networks of different security levels share the same Outer Encryption Component.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p022:u005.s0.text: Each Solution Component is described in more detail below.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p022:u006.s0.text: All the individual components within the solution must be physically protected to the level of the connected network with the highest classification/protection level.
The only exception to this requirement would be the Outer Firewall if one is present in the solution.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u002.s0.text: An MSC Solution that uses an untrusted network such as the Public Internet as its Black Network must include an Outer Firewall (see Section 4.
The Outer Firewall is located at the edge of the MSC Solution and is connected to the Black Network.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u003.s0.text: The external interface of the Outer Firewall only permits IPsec or MACsec traffic with a destination address of the Outer Encryption Component.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u004.s0.text: The internal interface of the Outer Firewall only permits IPsec or MACsec traffic with a source address of the Outer Encryption Component and any necessary control plane traffic.
The minimum requirements for port filtering on the Outer Firewall can be found in Section 10.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u005.s0.text: As shown in Figure 2, the Outer Firewall, selected from the CSfC Components List, must be physically separate from the Outer Encryption Component.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u007.s0.text: The Outer Encryption Component can be either a VPN Gateway or a MACsec Device.

The Outer Encryption Component establishes an encrypted tunnel using IPsec or MACsec with peer Outer Encryption Components, which provides device authentication, confidentiality, and integrity of information traversing Black Networks.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u008.s0.text: If the Black Network is the Public Internet, the external interface of the Outer Encryption Component is connected to the internal interface of the Outer Firewall.
Otherwise, the external interface of the Outer Encryption Component is connected to the Black Network.
The internal interface of the Outer Encryption Component is connected to Gray Firewalls, if required, or Inner Encryption Components.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u009.s0.text: The Outer Encryption Component may be a perimeter device (if the Outer Firewall is not present) and more exposed to external attacks.
The Outer Encryption Component may use internal filtering to help protect the network from unauthenticated traffic.

This CP does not require that the Outer Encryption Component terminate all tunnels on a single physical interface; however, all such external interfaces must conform to the port filtering requirements in Section 10.
The Outer Encryption Component is implemented identically for all the high-level designs covered in this CP.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u010.s0.text: Outer Encryption Components are also responsible for filtering traffic on its Gray Network interfaces to prevent Inner Encryption Components for networks of the same security level from being able to send packets to one another.

Since this filtering is primarily based on the source and destination addresses in the packet on a Gray Network, the Gray Network itself must use an addressing scheme that supports the necessary filtering (such as using separate address ranges for the Gray interfaces of Inner Encryption Components supporting each Red Network).

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p023:u011.s0.text: The Outer Encryption Component is prohibited from implementing routing protocols on external and internal interfaces and must rely on an Outer Firewall or Gray Firewall to provide dynamic routing functionality.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u001.s0.text: The Outer Encryption Component, selected from the CSfC Components List, must be physically separate from the Outer Firewall and Gray Firewall.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u002.s0.text: The Outer Encryption Component cannot route packets between Gray and Black Networks; any packets received on a Gray Network interface and sent out on a Black Network interface must be transmitted within an IPsec or MACsec tunnel configured according to this CP.
As described in this CP, Management traffic on a Gray Network, which originates from the AW, must include two layers of encryption.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u003.s0.text: For load balancing or other performance reasons, multiple Outer Encryption Components that comply with the requirements of this CP are acceptable.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u005.s0.text: The Gray Firewall is located between the Outer Encryption Component and Inner Encryption Component(s).
2, an MSC Solution that supports multiple Red Networks of different security levels must include one or more Gray Firewalls.
The Gray Firewall blocks any packets sent between Inner Encryption Components for Red Networks of different security levels.

A Gray Firewall also blocks any packets sent between management components on the Gray Network and Inner Encryption Components for Red Networks that operate at a security level other than the highest security level of data protected by the solution.
Gray Firewalls are physically protected as classified devices.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u006.s0.text: As shown in Figure 6, a standalone Gray Firewall, selected from the CSfC Components List, must be physically separate from the Outer Encryption Component and Inner Encryption Component.

A Gray Firewall would typically only be used in solutions where the physical design of the Gray Network includes paths between Inner Encryption Components for Red Networks of different security levels that do not pass through the Outer Encryption Components.
Effectively, each Gray Firewall is another instance of the Gray Network filtering performed by the Outer Encryption Component.
For load balancing or other performance reasons, multiple Gray Firewalls that comply with the requirements of this CP are acceptable.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u008.s0.text: Secure administration of components in the Gray Network and continuous monitoring of the Gray Network are essential roles provided by the Gray Management Services.
Gray Management Services are composed of multiple components that provide distinct security to the solution.
This CP allows flexibility in the placement of some Gray Management Services as described below.
The Gray Management Services are physically protected as classified devices.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u010.s0.text: The Gray AW maintains, monitors, and controls all security functionality for the Outer Encryption Component, Gray Firewall, and all Gray Management Service components.
The Gray AW is not permitted to maintain, monitor, or control Inner Encryption Components or Red Management Services.
All MSC Solutions must have at least one Gray AW.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u011.text: 5.4.2 GRAY SECURITY INFORMATION AND EVENT MANAGEMENT (SIEM)

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p024:u012.s0.text: The Gray SIEM collects and analyzes log data from the Outer Encryption Component, Gray Firewall, and other Gray Management Service components.
Log data should be encrypted between the originating component and the Gray SIEM with SSHv2, TLS 1.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u001.s0.text: The SIEM is configured to provide alerts for specific events including if the Outer Encryption Component or Gray Firewall receives and drops any unexpected traffic that could indicate a compromise.
These functions can also be performed on a Red SIEM using an approved CDS, as described in the CSfC Continuous Monitoring Annex.
A Gray SIEM is not a mandatory component of the MSC Solution.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u003.s0.text: Inner Encryption Components can either be VPN Gateways or MACsec Devices.
For load balance or other performance reasons, multiple Inner Encryption Components that comply with the requirements of this CP are acceptable.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u004.s0.text: Similar to an Outer Encryption Component, an Inner Encryption Component provides authentication of peer VPN Gateways or MACsec Devices, cryptographic protection of data in transit, and configuration and enforcement of network packet handling rules.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u005.s0.text: Similar to the Outer Encryption Component, the external interface of the Inner Encryption Component only permits egress of IPsec/MACsec traffic and AO-approved control plane traffic.
The internal interface of the Inner Encryption Component is configured to only permit traffic with an IP address and port associated with Red Network services.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u006.s0.text: The Inner Encryption Component must not route packets between Red and Gray Networks; any packets received on a Red Network interface and sent to a Gray Network interface must be transmitted within an IPsec or MACsec tunnel configured according to this CP.
The Inner Encryption Component, selected from the CSfC Components List, must be physically separate from the Gray Firewall and Inner Firewall, if either are required by this CP.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u007.s0.text: When an Inner MACsec Device is used, the MACsec traffic needs to be encapsulated prior to being processed by the Outer Encryption Component, regardless of whether it is a VPN Gateway or a MACsec Device.
Some VPN Gateways and MACsec Devices allow this encapsulation to occur on the incoming interface, prior to encrypting traffic for the outer tunnel.

If the selected VPN Gateway or MACsec Device does not have this feature, a separate standalone router or switch is necessary to provide encapsulation and all requirements for Solution Components in this CP must apply to it.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p025:u009.s0.text: An Inner Firewall is located between the Inner Encryption Component and the Red Network.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u005.text: MSC-IR-5 The Inner Encryption Component must not allow packets received on an interface connected to a Gray Network to bypass decryption and be forwarded out through an interface connected to a Red Network. T MSC-IR-6

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u006.text: MSC-IR-6 The Inner Encryption Component must use Mandatory Access Control policy to not allow packets received on an interface connected to a Gray Network to bypass decryption and be forwarded out through an interface connected to a Red Network. O MSC-IR-5

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u007.text: MSC-IR-7 The Inner Encryption Component must not permit split-tunneling. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u008.text: 10.5 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR OUTER ENCRYPTION COMPONENTS

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u009.s0.text: Table 15 defines additional Outer Encryption Components Requirements.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u012.text: MSC-OR-1 Outer VPN Gateways must use ESP Tunnel mode IPsec. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u013.text: MSC-OR-2 Outer Encryption Components must not allow packets received on an interface connected to a Gray Network to bypass encryption and be forwarded out through an interface connected to a Black Network. T MSC-OR-3

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p043:u014.text: MSC-OR-3 Outer Encryption Components must use Mandatory Access Control policy to not allow packets received on an interface connected to a Gray Network to O MSC-OR-2 bypass encryption and be forwarded out through an interface connected to a Black Network.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u003.text: MSC-OR-4 All traffic received by Outer Encryption Components on an interface connected to a Gray Network, with the exception of control plane traffic, must have already been encrypted once. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u004.text: MSC-OR-5 Outer Encryption Components must not allow any packets received on an interface connected to a Black Network to bypass decryption. T MSC-OR-6

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u005.text: MSC-OR-6 Outer Encryption Components must use Mandatory Access Control policy to not allow any packets received on an interface connected to a Black Network to bypass decryption. O MSC-OR-5

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u006.text: MSC-OR-7 The Outer Encryption Components must not permit split-tunneling. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u007.text: MSC-OR-8 Outer Encryption Components must not use routing protocols (e.g., OSPF, BGP). T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u008.text: MSC-OR-9 Outer Encryption must enable TRANSEC when external interface is MACsec enabled and connected to the Outer Firewall. O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u009.text: MSC-OR-10 Packets leaving the external interface of the Outer Encryption Component must only make connections with the remote Outer Encryption Component or the other intended device. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u011.s0.text: Table 16 defines Port Filtering Solution Components Requirements.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u014.text: MSC-PF-1 All Solution Components must have all network interfaces restricted to the smallest address ranges, ports, and protocols possible. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u015.text: MSC-PF-2 All Solution Components must have all unused network interfaces disabled. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u016.text: MSC-PF-3 For all Outer VPN Gateway interfaces connected to a Black Network, traffic filtering rules must be applied to both inbound and outbound traffic, such that only IKE, ESP, and control plane protocols (as defined in this CP) approved by organization-defined policy are allowed. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p044:u017.text: MSC-PF-4 For all Outer MACsec Device interfaces connected to a Black Network, traffic filtering rules must be T=O applied to both inbound and outbound traffic, such that only MACsec Protocol Data Units and control plane protocols (as defined in this CP) approved by organization-defined policy are allowed.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u003.text: MSC-PF-5 For all Inner Encryption Component interfaces connected to a Gray Network, traffic filtering rules must be applied to both inbound and outbound traffic, such that only IKE, IPsec, MKA, MACsec, and control plane protocols (as defined in this CP) approved by organization-defined policy are allowed. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u004.text: MSC-PF-6 Any service or feature that allows an Outer Encryption Component to contact a third-party server (such as one maintained by the manufacturer) must be blocked. T MSC-PF-7

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u005.text: MSC-PF-7 Any service or feature that allows an Outer Encryption Component to contact a third party server (such as one maintained by the manufacturer) must be disabled. O MSC-PF-6

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u006.text: MSC-PF-8 Management plane traffic must only be initiated from a Gray AW with the exception of logging or authentication traffic that may be initiated from Outer Encryption Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u007.text: MSC-PF-9 Multicast messages received on external interfaces of Outer Encryption Components must be dropped. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u008.text: MSC-PF-10 For solutions using IPv4, Outer VPN Gateways using IPsec must drop all packets that use IP options. O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u009.text: MSC-PF-11 For solutions using IPv4, each VPN Gateway must only accept packets with Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), User Datagram Protocol (UDP), ESP, or ICMP in the IPv4 Protocol field and drop all other packets. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u010.text: MSC-PF-12 For solutions using IPv6, each VPN Gateway must only accept packets with ESP, TCP, UDP, or ICMPv6 in the IPv6 Next Header field and drop all other packets. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u011.text: MSC-PF-13 The Gray Network interfaces of Outer Encryption Components must allow IKE and IPsec, or MKA and MACsec traffic, as appropriate, between two Inner Encryption Components protecting networks of the same security level or that is being used for management of the Gray Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p045:u013.text: MSC-PF-15 If the CDP/OCSP is on the gray data plane, the Gray Network interfaces of Outer VPN Gateways must T=O allow HTTP traffic that is necessary to perform revocation checking for the Inner encryption layer (i.e., requests/replies between the Inner VPN Gateways and the CDPs/OCSP Responders) and block all other HTTP traffic. Refer to IETF RFC 5280 and IETF RFC 6960 for further details on this type of traffic.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u004.text: MSC-PF-17 The Gray Network interfaces of Outer Encryption Components must only permit packets whose source and destination IP addresses match the external interfaces of Inner Encryption Components that support Red Networks of the same security level. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u005.text: MSC-PF-18 The Gray Network interfaces of Outer Encryption Components must block all packets whose source address does not match a list of addresses or address ranges known to be reachable from the interface where the packet was received. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u006.text: MSC-PF-19 The Gray Network interfaces of Outer Encryption Components must allow management and control plane protocols (as defined in this CP) that have been approved by policy. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u007.text: MSC-PF-20 The Gray Network interfaces of Outer Encryption Components must deny all traffic that is not explicitly allowed by requirements MSC-PF-8, MSC- PF-13, MSC-PF-15, or MSC-PF-19. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u009.text: MSC-PF-22 If an Outer Firewall is required, for all Outer Firewall interfaces, traffic filtering rules must be applied to both inbound and outbound traffic, such that only IKE, ESP, MKA, MACsec and control plane protocols (as defined in this CP) approved by organization- defined policy are allowed. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u010.text: MSC-PF-23 If a Gray Firewall is required (i.e., networks of multiple protection levels are included in the solution) the Gray Firewall must allow appropriate traffic (IKE, IPsec, MKA and MACsec) between Red Networks operating at the same security level. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p046:u012.text: MSC-PF-25 If a Gray Firewall is required, the Gray Firewall must allow HTTP traffic that is necessary to perform revocation checking for the Inner encryption layer (i.e., requests/replies between the Inner VPN Gateways and CDPs/OCSP Responders) and block all T=O other HTTP traffic. Refer to IETF RFC 5280 and IETF RFC 6960 for further details on this type of traffic.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u004.text: MSC-PF-27 If a Gray Firewall is required, the Gray Firewall must only accept management traffic on the physical ports connected to the Gray Management Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u005.text: MSC-PF-28 If a Gray Firewall is required, the Gray Firewall must only permit packets whose source and destination IP addresses match the external interfaces of Inner Encryption Components that support Red Networks of the same security level. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u006.text: MSC-PF-29 If a Gray Firewall is required, the Gray Firewall must block all packets whose source address does not match a list of addresses or address ranges known to be reachable from the interface where the packet was received. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u007.text: MSC-PF-30 If a Gray Firewall is required, the Gray Firewall must allow control plane traffic (e.g., NTP and DHCP). T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u008.text: MSC-PF-31 If a Gray Firewall is required, the Gray Firewall must deny all traffic that is not explicitly allowed by requirements MSC-PF-23, MSC-PF-25, MSC-PF-27 or MSC-PF-30. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u009.text: MSC-PF-32 The Gray Firewall must block all traffic routed to and between two or more Inner VPN Gateways of different classification levels. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u016.text: MSC-DM-1 If using physical AWs, they must be dedicated for the purposes given in this CP and must be physically separated from workstations used to manage non-CSfC solutions. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p047:u017.text: MSC-DM-2 AWs (or hosts/servers hosting VMs serving as AWs) must physically reside within a protected facility where CSfC solution(s) are managed. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u002.text: MSC-DM-3 AWs must connect from an internal port. Specifically, the Inner Encryption Component must be managed from the Red Network, and the Outer Encryption Component and Gray Firewall, if present, must be managed from the Gray Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u003.text: MSC-DM-4 The Red Management Network must be used exclusively for all management of Inner Encryption Components and Solution Components within the Red Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u004.text: MSC-DM-5 The Gray Network must be used exclusively for all management of the Outer Encryption Component, Gray Firewall, if present, and Solution Components within the Gray Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u006.text: MSC-DM-7 All components must be configured to restrict the IP address range for the network administration device to the smallest range possible. Note that locally managing Solution Components is also acceptable. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u007.text: MSC-DM-8 All administration of Solution Components must securely be performed from an AW remotely using an NSA-approved solution (e.g., CP or High Assurance encryptor), or by managing the Solution Components locally. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u008.text: MSC-DM-9 Security Administrators must authenticate to Solution Components before performing administrative functions. T MSC-DM-10

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u009.text: MSC-DM-10 Security Administrators must authenticate to Solution Components with CNSA Suite compliant certificates before performing administrative functions. O MSC-DM-9

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p048:u011.text: MSC-DM-12 Authorized Security Administrators must initiate certificate signing requests for Solution Components as part of their initial keying within the solution. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u002.text: MSC-DM-14 AWs that interact with the Certificate Authority for the Outer VPN Gateways must be located on the Gray Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u005.text: MSC-DM-17 The same AW must not be used to manage Inner Encryption Components and Outer Encryption Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u010.text: MSC-DM-22 Outer Encryption Components must only be managed by Security Administrators cleared to at least the highest level of classification of each Red Network supported by the Outer Encryption Component at the physical site the Outer Encryption Component is located. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u011.text: MSC-DM-23 Hosts/servers for management VMs may not host VMs that perform non-CSfC functions. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u012.text: MSC-DM-24 VMs that perform management services must not also perform other functions within the solution (i.e., provisioning, enrollment, CA registration, SIEM, etc. must be performed by separate workstations or VMs). T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u013.text: MSC-DM-25 The Gray Management and Gray Data Networks must be at minimum logically separated by the Gray Firewall using ACL. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u014.text: MSC-DM-26 AWs (physical or virtual) must be configured, patched, and operated in accordance with applicable Operating System vendor hardening guide and the organizational or local policy. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u015.text: MSC-DM-27 AWs (physical or virtual) must be powered off when not in use. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u016.text: MSC-DM-28 The AW must not also be used for provisioning, certificate registrations, and SIEM services. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p049:u017.text: MSC-DM-29 Each AW admin must have a unique login credential. Group accounts are prohibited. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p050:u013.text: MSC-GD-1 All Solution Components, with the exception of the Outer Firewall (if present), must be physically protected as classified devices, classified at the level of the network with the highest classification in the solution or in any other MSC Solutions with which it is interconnected. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p050:u014.text: MSC-GD-2 Only authorized and appropriately cleared (or escorted) administrators and security personnel must have physical access to the Solution Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p052:u003.text: MSC-GD-21 All infrastructure components must implement a password of at least 112 random bits. Passwords should be generated using an approved password generator. See CSfC Key Management Requirements Annex, Appendix A for more information. T MSC-GD-27

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p052:u005.text: MSC-GD-23 Local policy must dictate how the Security Administrator installs patches to Solution Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p052:u006.text: MSC-GD-24 Solution Components must comply with local TEMPEST policy. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p052:u009.text: MSC-GD-27 All infrastructure components must use an authentication service on their respective network/domain in order to access the Infrastructure component of the respective network/domain. O MSC-GD-21

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p053:u005.text: MSC-RP-3 Solution Owners must report a security failure in any of the CSfC Solution Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p053:u009.text: MSC-RP-7 Solution Owners must report if a Solution Component sends traffic with an unauthorized destination address. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p053:u011.text: MSC-RP-9 Solution Owners must report any unauthorized escalation of privileges to any of the CSfC Solution Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p053:u013.text: MSC-RP-11 Solution Owners must report any evidence of malicious physical tampering with Solution Components. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p055:u013.text: MSC-RB-5 The Security Administrator(s) for the Inner Encryption Components and supporting components on the Red Network must be different individuals from the Security Administrator(s) for the Outer Encryption Components and supporting components on the Gray Network. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p055:u014.text: MSC-RB-6 Administrators must periodically inspect the physical attributes of infrastructure hardware for signs of tampering or other unauthorized changes. T=O

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p059:u010.s0.text: Central Management Site – A site within a MSC Solution that is responsible for remotely managing the Solution Components located at other sites.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p059:u011.s0.text: Certification Authority (CA) – An authority trusted by one or more users to create and assign certificates.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u001.s0.text: CRL Distribution Point (CDP) – A web server that hosts a copy of a CRL issued by a CA for VPN Gateways to download (see CSfC Key Management Requirements Annex).

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u002.s0.text: Cross Domain Solution (CDS) – A form of controlled interface that provides the ability to manually and/or automatically access and/or transfer information between different security domains.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u004.s0.text: Encryption Component – Either a VPN Gateway or a MACsec Device.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u005.s0.text: External Interface – The interface on an Encryption Component that connects to the outer network (i.
, the Gray Network on the Inner Encryption Component or the Black Network on the Outer Encryption Component).

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u007.s0.text: In addition, the use of any and all testing equipment and/or testing software used inside and outside the developed solution is available.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u009.s0.text: Gray Firewall – A traffic filtering firewall placed on the Gray Network to provide additional separation between flows of singly-encrypted data of different security levels.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u010.s0.text: Independently Managed Site – A site within a MSC Solution where Solution Components are locally managed and that does not remotely manage other sites’ Solution Components.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u012.s0.text: Internal Interface – The interface on an Encryption Component that connects to the inner network (i.
, the Gray Network on the Outer Encryption Component or the Red Network on the Inner Encryption Component).

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u013.s0.text: Key Server – The MACsec Device designated as the one responsible for distribution Secure Association Keys to the other MACsec Device.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p060:u014.s0.text: Locally Managed Device – A device that is being managed by the direct connection of the AW to the device in a hardwired fashion (such as a console cable).

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p061:u005.s0.text: Registration Authority (RA) – An entity authorized by the CA to collect, verify, and submit information that is to be entered into public key certificates.
The term RA refers to hardware, software, and individuals that collectively perform this function.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p061:u006.s0.text: Remotely Managed Device – A device that is being managed by any other method besides that given in the definition of a Locally Managed Device.

CSFC-MSC-1.3.0-4e40e3d83708:p061:u007.s0.text: Remote Site – A site within a MSC Solution where Solution Components are remotely managed by a Central Management Site.
